result.decision_rationale: Both pending findings are resolved. The focused gate passed, and the simulated session establishes that ordinary weapon prices and tooltips survive failed initialization. One product defect still blocks readiness. The spear validator can accept an extra effective weapon classification that violates the released profile.

executed_verification: The controller receipt records production compilation and 27 of 27 selected elven-branched-spear tests passing on 77478c375edc in 2.4 seconds. The worktree was unchanged.

The recorded report for simulated session 20261121T171410Z identifies package f8988fde…bbbb00, product DLL f0f17f7c…ab574 and harness be0d9e79…2b8e. The session passed. Registry restoration and the checks for unchanged owner saves and installation all returned true.

The S-2 harness result records 25 price queries and 25 tooltip fills apiece for Longspear, Longsword, Greataxe and Heavy Crossbow. Prices were 1, 4, 5 and 13 gp with matching tooltip text and zero throws. The session PASS also enforces S-2’s exactly-one unavailable warning and zero missing-token messages.

The transcript truncates the middle launch rows of the simulated-session report. The stored aggregate PASS, final launch numbered 12, unchanged session definition and runner verdict logic establish the required assertions. Only visible rows and per-launch excerpts were read directly.
The reviewer performed read-only inspection. The native runs used the identified development package. The final commit received the focused gate.
required_gaps: The effective subcategory check does not cover classifications outside its two hard-coded lists. A focused native control for an unexpected granted classification is needed after correction.
source_inspection_only: The omitted-category defect follows from the inputs to SubCategoryList and the released category policy. The existing S-12 run exercises removal of a listed classification.
The revised persistence comment matches the fixture and reload implementation. The strict battered-item creation and ownership paths and the summoning publication guards were also inspected.

findings.actual: SubCategoryList queries only IntendedSubCategories and ExcludedSubCategories. Simple is in neither list, although docs/ELVEN-BRANCHED-SPEAR-IMPLEMENTATION-EVIDENCE.md identifies it as a distinct native classification. A postfix that adds only Simple produces identical expected and observed strings, so validation passes. The lists also omit the existing HasSubCategory(None) wildcard contract.
findings.blocking_rationale: Initialization can succeed and publish selectors while native consumers see an exotic spear classified as Simple. That contradicts the fixed profile and the requirement to fail visibly for an incorrect owned spear.
findings.expected: The registered spear’s effective HasSubCategory results agree with its fixed policy across the supported classifications. A discrepancy identifies the unexpected result and the implicated patch owners.
findings.requested_correction: Compare the registered category’s effective membership across the supported WeaponSubCategory values. Preserve the separate None wildcard behavior and the five concrete intended classifications. Keep donor context and patch-owner reporting on mismatch.
findings.requested_evidence: Use the isolated native harness to grant Simple only to the registered spear while retaining all five intended classifications. Show one diagnostic naming the extra classification and patch owner, with selectors restored. Retain the healthy spear and Finessable-removal controls.
findings.title: The effective profile can pass with an extra weapon classification
findings.trigger: A late HasSubCategory postfix grants Simple to the released spear and leaves the currently checked classifications unchanged.

findings.blocking_rationale: The session verdict, restoration flags and S-2 observations used in this review remain interpretable. The issue affects the report’s reliability for machine readers.
findings.expected: Array-valued fields retain their JSON type and cardinality in the read-only report.
findings.requested_correction: Preserve arrays when projecting report fields, including empty and single-element arrays.
findings.requested_evidence: A read-only serialization check showing problems as [] and a single active mod as a one-element array is sufficient.
findings.title: The report changes the JSON shape of short arrays
findings.trigger: A reported field such as problems, activeMods or steps contains zero or one entry.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The transcript now contains machine-produced session identity, aggregate verdict and restoration fields, plus the S-2 per-weapon results. The runner requires every launch to pass its identity, harness and log assertions before the session can pass. Together with the retained diagnostic excerpts, this closes the evidence gap.
The persistence comment now describes blueprint identities, inventory counts and the battered owner’s character ID. Those are the values the fixture writes and the reload probe checks.

summary.delivered_behavior: The repair explicitly configures the owned spear, validates its effective values after GUID assignment, and keeps ordinary weapon inspection usable after failed startup. Native evidence covers the simulated donor mutation, normal and battered pricing, disabled-publication reload, and a usable Summon Monster I menu with a successful selected summon.
